entities.summary: Eminönü, historically known as Pérama, is a predominantly commercial waterfront area of Istanbul within the Fatih district near the confluence of the Golden Horn with the southern entrance of the Bosphorus strait and the Sea of Marmara. It is located in the part of Istanbul known as the historical peninsula, connected to Karaköy via the Galata Bridge across the Golden Horn. It was administered as part of the Sultanahmet district from 1928 to 2009 when Sultanahmet was absorbed into Fatih. Eminönü, which was a district municipality until March 7, 2008, was abolished on this date and connected to Fatih district by law.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Eminönü's strategic location facilitated trade and cultural exchange between East and West during the Byzantine Empire, with its bustling markets and warehouses serving as a hub for commerce and intellectual discourse. Its historical significance as a crossroads of civilizations underscores the importance of this waterfront area in shaping Istanbul's identity.
